pslBCD is required for antibiotic tolerance of P. aeruginosa in the presence and absence of a biofilm, that psl is activated by surface adherence and c-di-GMP and that psl is a target for the development of antimicrobial agents against P. aeruginasa.
pslBCD, which is regulated by intracellular c-diGMP levels and activated by surface adherence, is essential for antibiotic tolerance.
pslBCD is required to mediate antibiotic tolerance of adherent P. aeruginosa cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genetic determinants of antibiotic tolerance in adherent P. aeruginosa cells.
the identification of genes involved in antibiotic tolerance in adherent bacterial cells.
the role of pslBCDE in antibiotic tolerance in adherent P. aeruginosa cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the psl operon, in conjunction with c-di-GMP signaling, is essential for the tolerance of adherent P. aeruginosa cells to biapenen and other antibiotics.
the psl operon, which is activated by surface adherence, confers antibiotic tolerance in biofilms.
the pslBCD genes play an important role in mediating antibiotic tolerance in adherent P. aeruginosa cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pslBCD genes are essential for the tolerance of P. aeruginosa to biapenems and tobramycins, and this effect is mediated by c-di-GMP and the Psl polysaccharide.
we have identified a novel mechanism of antibiotic tolerance, and the mechanism involves the polysaccharides Psl and Pel and the c-di-GMP signaling pathway.
the pslBCD genes, which are directly involved in polysaccharide synthesis, confer tolerance to antibiotics in adherent cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pseudomonas biofilm polysaccharide, psl, is an important factor in antibiotic tolerance of adherent cells.
the psl operon is a key determinant of the antibiotic-tolerant phenotype.
the polysaccharides produced by the psl genes are important for tolerance of P. aeruginosa to antibiotics.
